script.base: No spread or total is saved, so this is a form script, not a book script. MIN has been run-leaning (A.Jones 35/145, J.Mason 15/59, C.Wentz 5/8 over weeks 1-2) with J.Jefferson the only high-volume receiver (15 targets, 147 yards). TB has been balanced: B.Irving 25/134 rush plus 11 targets, B.Mayfield 8/60 rush, and five pass-catchers between 7 and 11 targets. Both offenses grade better when blitzed (MIN EPA/db +0.10 vs blitz, -0.04 vs none; TB +0.02 vs blitz, -0.33 vs none) and both defenses blitz (TB 49%, MIN 78%). Base case: a competitive pressure game. MIN tries to run Jones into TB's stingier run defense (3.26 YPC, only 4 runs of 10+) with C Nick Samac out, so the run may stall and Jefferson/Hockenson/Oliver see the middle. TB attacks the 78% blitz with Irving checkdowns (11 targets, -47 air yards) and Mayfield scrambles, while both middles leak (TB 12.4 YPA on 10 att, MIN 10.58 YPA on 19 att).
script.flip1: MIN leads and clocks with Jones (the 105-yard path). Irving's late carries die and TB's pass-catchers (E.Egbuka 159 air, T.Hurst 179 air, C.Otton) absorb the dropbacks. Irving still has a receiving path; a pure Jones-clock game is the kill for a TB rush-only leg.
script.flip2: TB leads, MIN abandons the run (Jones's 40-yard game), and Wentz funnels to Jefferson (15 targets) and T.Hockenson (9). Irving's carries go up late. Oliver's short targets can survive because a trailing MIN still throws.

pre_mortem: It's Monday and this lost. Oliver: the two backup linebackers still sat on the TE, he saw one target or none (only 5 targets in two games), and 10.5 needs a catch he did not get. The coin-flip 10.5 line means the market never believed the 22/24 role, and those games may have been softer shells than this one. Irving: neither spike showed up. Twelve carries at 3.85 YPC is about 48 rush yards, the checkdowns gained the 1-yard game instead of the 48-yard game, and 48+1 loses by a lot to 77.5. Or TB got ahead, Irving was spelled by Gainwell (7 carries already), and the starters' late snaps died. The 93 and 90 were two different outliers, not a stable 90-yard floor. If that quiet-both-paths case is the one you trust more than the blitz-plus-explosive overlap, drop Irving and keep only Oliver as a flagged lean-to-strong for the human.
slip_story: One pressure-and-middle story, not a total stack (total unknown) and not a TD slip. MIN's 78% blitz feeds Irving's checkdown or explosive dual role; TB's missing linebackers and middle YPA feed Oliver's short TE work. They do not need the same winner. They lose together only if MIN goes pure clock-run and TB's blitz checkdowns and explosive runs both disappear. Two legs, one market per player, no depth WR, no pass yards. Not a bet to place.
